title: A Parent’s Heart
text: “Grr… bro! No, wait, Sword Bro! Is that really okay?! Wolf Bro!”
“Ahh…”
Ren glanced awkwardly toward Father. It was the same expression he wore whenever Kuro-chan latched onto him. He seemed to have at least sensed the mood, I’ll give him that.
“Those who hold power must sometimes remove the discordant elements that disturb the harmony. Wof.”
Wolf, apparently also grasping the situation, had joined in trying to talk sense into Keel.
“Come on! What about Luna-chan? You can’t just say ‘because it’s a dragon’ and leave it at that!”
“Hmm… if Keel-kun asked, would Luna catch the dragon and beat it until it brings that girl back?”
“That’s… probably not okay, is it.”
Father cut in and scooped Keel up into his arms.
“What the heck, bro! Let go! It’s not fair to Wyndia-chan! She didn’t even do anything wrong!”
“Well, you see…”
Father leaned in close to Keel’s ear and explained the situation in a hushed voice.

Then, as if to seal the secret further, he pressed a finger to his own lips. I recognized that gesture as one of Father’s gentle habits. It gave me a rather bittersweet feeling, I say. And with that, Rival’s parent simply took flight and departed.
“Aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaah!!”
Left behind, Assistant wailed as though her very heart were breaking. After a while, Father spoke to her.
“Wyndia-chan. You don’t really have anywhere else to go, so… would you come stay with us? Keel-kun’s there too. Why don’t you live with everyone for a while and think about what comes next?”
“Sniff…”
“You can’t stay here like this, and it’s dangerous for you to be alone, you know?”

It was doubtful whether Assistant was even listening to Father’s proposal, but she kept crying regardless, until eventually, worn out, she fell asleep. Well, this was more or less the standard procedure whenever Rival’s parent entrusted Assistant to Father. Though… it really was remarkable how consistently this ended with Father taking custody. When I was the one who’d thrashed it, it never once handed her over to me, indeed. Strange, that. In any case, Father ended up carrying the sleeping Assistant on his back as we made our way down the mountain.
When we descended the mountain, the villagers came out to greet us.
“No one has gone missing from this village…”
“Boo.”
“Ah, she’s not from your village—turns out she was a slave from ours. We found her like this.”
“I-I see. So then… since dragons inhabit the mountain, did you happen to… encounter one?”
“…No, we didn’t. So none of my slaves were injured either.”
Father lied smoothly, without missing a beat.
“I-I see. That’s good to hear.”

These were the sort of people who’d rushed to loot treasure the moment Ren finished off Rival’s parent, after all. Perhaps Father was being careful not to give them any opening to exploit. Or maybe he’d read between the lines—that they were probably hoping some demi-human or beastman had gotten hurt. Supposedly there was a fair amount of trade with this village, which apparently made it slightly less prejudiced than most—about the only redeeming quality it had.
“Well then, I’m sorry to have caused trouble on what should’ve been a festive occasion. Please come see the circus tomorrow if you’d like.”
“Y-yes.”
And so we laid the sleeping Assistant down on a bed in the wagon parked behind the circus tent.
“Now then…”
“Bro. Are you seriously taking Wyndia-chan with us?”

“She was asked to be taken care of, after all. That dragon—even though its bond with her was supposed to be nothing more than a brief encounter—still came all the way to a region crawling with dangerous dragons just to help. I wanted to entrust Wyndia-chan to someone like that.”
You did good, Father said, patting Keel’s head.
“It’s because I made a big fuss over nothing that Wyndia-chan’s favorite… um…”

“It’s precisely because she’s precious to it. That dragon—Father Dragon, I mean—cares deeply for Wyndia-chan. Being together isn’t always the only path to happiness, you know… It did this because it cares.”
“Uuu…”
Keel’s reaction made it clear she wasn’t entirely convinced.
“It was a parent’s heart, thinking that staying at the dragon’s nest forever wouldn’t be good for Wyndia-chan. Honestly… that one hit a little close to home for me too.”

Now that I thought about it, Father had once mentioned that back in Japan, his parents had mostly left him to his own devices, only spoiling him at key moments. By his own self-deprecating account, he’d lived something like a NEET, F-rank sort of lazy existence. But now, I could say with certainty—that was absolutely not the case. He’d apparently worked all sorts of part-time jobs, and acquaintances had told him they wanted to hire him properly in the future, or so he’d mentioned. Even someone as dense as I’m often accused of being could tell that Father was nothing like society’s so-called “lazy people.” Among the lazy pigs, there’d been one running some mysterious business venture, and it was easy to imagine Father having been far more active than that. Above all, there was no way someone more energetic than Lazy Pig herself could possibly be called lazy. According to Ren, Father had once been dubbed “a slave among slaves,” indeed.
“A girl raised by a dragon, is it… My, what a story that makes.”
Rabbit Guy’s eyes lit up at the mention of Assistant’s backstory.
“I suppose from Theo’s perspective it sounds like quite the wonderful upbringing?”
“Indeed—forgive my saying so, but it’s rather like something out of a tale… By the way, she’s not his biological daughter, is she? She doesn’t have any dragon features.”
“Right. Seems like fate brought them together somehow, and he raised her as his own.”
“Well now… Still, I find myself quite curious how a child raised this way might turn out. For instance, might there be a story like ‘what if Iwatani-sama had never met Shion, Wolf, and I’?”
Rabbit Guy seemed to be subtly fishing for information from Father.
“There might be something to that. What do you think, Motoyasu-kun?”
“Indeed. Surely Ren has some idea how it might go, wouldn’t you say?”
I tossed the question straight at Ren.
“…No idea. And frankly, there’s no point exploring such possibilities!”
Ren, suddenly put on the spot, flatly refused to engage.
“You did warn her not to go into the mountains, after all… I see, so it came back to bite you.”
“I said I have no idea!”
Ren had probably already pieced together the implications from the exchange between Assistant and Rival’s parent. And don’t think I didn’t notice him breathing a sigh of relief just now.

“In that case, the possible future would be: her parent slain, the nest’s treasure stolen, her siblings killed, reduced to slavery, only to grow strong enough to try and kill the hero… A tragic avenger, perhaps?”
Wrong, I say. Well, there’s certainly a recurring loop where Ren gets thrashed, but it’s never gone as far as killing him.
“Wof.”
Hey now, Wolf, why are you looking at me like that? Sure, I’ve slain a great many dragons who stood as enemies of Filolial-sama, but I’ve never once killed Rival’s parent.
“Eh? Is someone gonna kill Wyndia-chan’s dad?”
Keel, ever slow on the uptake, asked Father directly.

“Ah, it’d be Spear Bro, wouldn’t it! No matter how much the Filolials hate dragons, you can’t go doing something that awful! If you’re planning on going after it, I’m stopping you right now. Luna and the others would get yelled at by you guys too if they ever did something like that, so don’t!”
“Luna wouldn’t do that~”
“I’ve never done such a thing, I say.”
“Is that so? Even after slaughtering so many of them with me in tow?”
Rabbit Guy was being awfully loud about it.
“Is it not true?” even Crocodile Guy, who’d come back into the tent, asked me.
“Being blamed for everything is most unjust, I say! I am innocent, indeed!”
“Your usual conduct makes you an easy suspect. In any case, Iwatani-sama—so you’ve been entrusted with that girl, then?”
“Yeah. Various circumstances, really—well, mostly because Keel-kun’s taken such a liking to her that I was asked.”

“I see. To entrust her to you after being thrashed that badly—either it knows its place, or it recognized the Shield Hero as a man of character. Foresight, perhaps—a keen eye for spotting treasure, wouldn’t you say?”
Dragons were typically associated with demon lords and villainy, but Rabbit Guy nodded along, remarking that this sort of story had its own dramatic flair.
